features.t: Users (create, get, list, update, delete) over Microsoft Graph
Groups (create, get, list, delete, membership) over Microsoft Graph
x: Dynamic membership rules are stored but never evaluated — Vyomi only tracks membership added/removed explicitly.

features.t: App registrations, their auto-created enterprise application (service principal), and client secrets
x: Only the default Microsoft Graph User.Read delegated permission is seeded on every new registration; the API permissions / admin-consent workflow and OAuth2 token issuance are not simulated.
Added domains are never verified (isVerified stays false) — Vyomi has no DNS/TXT-record check to perform.

features.t: Roles and administrators (built-in + custom directory roles, assignments)
x: Shares its evaluation engine with Azure RBAC (Microsoft.Authorization); directory roles are modelled as role definitions assignable at the tenant-root scope rather than through the real roleManagement/directory Graph surface.
Only console/API-triggered directory mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); category/activity filtering and the date-range picker are not modelled.

features.t: Tenant properties (name, technical/privacy contacts, verified domains)
User settings (default user role permissions, guest access, LinkedIn connections)
x: 'Users can create security groups' = No really blocks POST /v1.0/groups for security groups (Microsoft 365 groups are unaffected); 'Users can register applications' = No really blocks POST /v1.0/applications — both return Graph's 403 Authorization_RequestDenied.

Service principal sign-ins are real: POST /{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/token validates the caller's actual client secret (set by addPassword/removePassword on the app, core/azure_graph_core.py) and appends a success or failure row for that exact attempt — never sample data.

features.t: Security defaults / Access management for Azure resources
x: 'Access management for Azure resources' = Yes really grants a tenant-root (scope "/") 'User Access Administrator' role assignment over the same Azure RBAC checkAccess engine every subscription's Access control (IAM) page uses — the real console's elevateAccess action. It is modelled for the single caller identity Vyomi has (no signed-in-admin model), not per-signed-in-user.

features.t: Devices (registration, inventory, a user's registered devices)
x: Registration, listing and deletion of real device objects (GET/POST /v1.0/users/{id}/registeredDevices, GET/DELETE /v1.0/devices/{id}) is real and enforced — the Devices overview's alert counts and 'Download devices' export read this same live inventory, not stored config.
Fixed three-SKU catalogue (Entra ID P1, P2, Office 365 E3) with prepaid unit counts; no billing, no group-based licensing, service-plan toggles are stored only.

features.t: Conditional Access policies, named locations and What If evaluation
x: Evaluated for users/groups, applications, IP locations, platform, risk levels and client app types; enforced only on the password (ROPC) token grant, as there is no interactive sign-in. Device-compliance, session controls and authentication strengths are stored but not evaluated against a real device.

features.t: Custom security attributes: attribute sets, definitions, user assignment
x: Assignment on users is validated against definitions; service-principal assignment and attribute-based access conditions in RBAC are not modelled.
Membership is stored and listed; scoped role assignments over an AU are not enforced.
Enforced state makes the password grant fail with AADSTS50076; no authenticator enrolment exists.
Up to 20 requests per batch, executed sequentially; dependsOn is ignored.
